properties.areaDesc: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 19 at 9:55PM PDT until October 20 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves. Surf of 3 to 6
feet with local sets as high as 7 feet. Highest surf on south
and southwest facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County coastal areas and Orange County
coastal areas.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Areas of hazardous swimming conditions. Rip currents
can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash
people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion may occur across
south- facing beaches.
properties.instruction: Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

NWSheadline: BEACH HAZARDS STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH TUESDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Anchorage; Lower Matanuska Valley; Sutton / Upper Matanuska Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 19 at 8:52PM AKDT until October 20 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 2 and 6
inches, highest amounts near the mountains.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of Anchorage and the Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...From 4 AM to 1 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads. Visibilities as low as one half mile possible, including
during the morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Rain will intensify during the overnight hours
and change to  snow late tonight through early Tuesday morning,
with temperatures falling to near freezing. The heaviest snow and
highest accumulation will be near the mountains, from the lower
Anchorage Hillside to East Anchorage and up the Glenn Highway
corridor to Palmer and Sutton. Roads will start out wet and road
surface temperatures are still warm (in the upper 30s), but steady
moderate snow should be enough to lead to slushy accumulation,
especially along neighborhood roads. Snow will change back to rain
by late morning in south to west Anchorage, continue northward to
the Matanuska Valley in the afternoon. The exact timing of
changeover back to rain will greatly impact total snow amounts.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

properties.description:
Relative Humidities of less than 30 percent can be expected for 4
or more hours this afternoon into the evening. Winds will be North

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 19 at 8:48PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 3 and 7
inches.

* WHERE...Fairbanks, Fox, Chatanika, Ester and Nenena.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Light snow is expected Monday night. Heavier
snow is expected Tuesday. There is high uncertainty in the exact
location of this heavier snow area. This detail will be crucial in
determining which spots get 6 inches or more versus 3 inches or
less. A 30 mile change east or west will result in drastic
differences. If the area of heavier snow shifts slightly west,
heavy snow becomes more likely over the area. If the area of
heavier snow shifts slightly east, heavy snow becomes less likely
over the area.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. Visit 511.alaska.gov or
call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 19 at 8:48PM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 6 to 12
inches expected, with 1 to 3 inches expected from Northway to the
Alcan Border along the Alaska Highway. Locally higher snow totals
of 12 to 16 inches will be possible, especially between Tanacross
and Dot Lake. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph. Rain may mix with
snow in the Upper Tanana Valley around Northway to the Alcan
Border.

* WHERE...Delta Junction, Fortymile Country, and Upper Tanana Valley.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Northwest wind gusts may be as high as 35 mph
Tuesday morning through early Wednesday morning.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, water, and warm
clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 5 to 10
inches expected. Wind could gust as high as 35 mph across higher
elevations.

* WHERE...Upper Chena River Valley, Southern and Eastern Yukon Flats,
White Mountains, and Eagle Summit.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could reduce visibility below one half
mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be a narrow snow gradient. The
highest potential for heaviest snow lies southeast of Fort Yukon.
West and north of there, the likelihood for heavier snow drops
quickly. Locations near Beaver and Livengood may end up getting
closer to 2 to 4 inches or less.

clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

inches. Winds gusting as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...Denali Borough.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Tuesday to 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...North and west of Healy, the chance for heavy
snow drops off quickly due to a narrow gradient of snow. There is
potential for greater than 6 inches in Healy but only a few inches
in Anderson. The exact placement of the area of heavier will have a
dramatic effect on the final snowfall totals. If the band moves a
few dozen miles west, snowfall totals will be on the higher end of
the range, especially near Healy. If the band moves a few dozen
miles east, snowfall totals will likely be on the lower end, even
in Healy.

properties.areaDesc: Dixon Entrance to Cape Decision out to 15 NM
properties.headline: Gale Warning issued October 19 at 8:14PM AKDT until October 20 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the first Small Craft Advisory, south winds 25 to 30
kt with gusts up to 45 kt and seas 12 to 17 ft expected. For the
Gale Warning, south winds 30 to 40 kt with gusts up to 45 kt
and seas 13 to 18 ft expected. For the second Small Craft
Advisory, seas 10 to 15 ft expected.

* WHERE...Dixon Entrance to Cape Decision out to 15 NM.

* WHEN...For the first Small Craft Advisory, from 1 AM to 10 AM
AKDT Tuesday. For the Gale Warning, from 10 AM to 10 PM AKDT
Tuesday. For the second Small Craft Advisory, from 10 PM
Tuesday to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
properties.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for hazardous conditions.
